inputs.name: NativeHandoffController.constructor.options
inputs.description: The two services the controller delegates to: `handoff`, a NativeHandoffService that all four routes use, and `sessions`, a RequestSessionService whose browser() supplies the cookie session that only approve uses. The constructor stores both references without checking them.

outputs.name: NativeHandoffController.routes
outputs.description: The route table from routes(), keyed by `POST /api/auth/native/start`, `POST /api/auth/native/approve`, `POST /api/auth/native/poll` and `POST /api/auth/native/exchange`; each handler takes a Request and resolves to a JSON Response. Input values come only from an application/json body of at most 16384 bytes, never from the URL, and known failures reject with the AuthFailure codes listed under errors.

errors.name: AuthFailure
errors.description: Thrown as an AuthFailure with code `invalid-request` (HTTP 400) on any route when readJson refuses the body: a media type other than application/json, more than 16384 bytes, text that is not UTF-8, or JSON that is not an object. It is also thrown when a required field is missing or does not match its expected format.

errors.name: AuthFailure
errors.description: Thrown as an AuthFailure with code `session-required` (HTTP 401) by RequestSessionService.browser(), which approve calls first, when the request carries an Authorization header (only a browser session may approve) or no live browser session cookie resolves.

errors.name: AuthFailure
errors.description: Thrown as an AuthFailure with code `origin-denied` (HTTP 403) by RequestSessionService.browser() when a request without an Authorization header fails the sameOrigin check against the configured origin. POST is not a safe method, so approve always gets this check.

errors.name: AuthFailure
errors.description: Thrown as an AuthFailure with code `handoff-invalid` (HTTP 400) by NativeHandoffService.approve() when the store does not approve the handoff or cannot read it back, and by NativeHandoffService.exchange() when its claim returns no record, a binding check fails (verifier, nonce, resource, audience, action, environment or origin), or the approving session is not a live browser session of the same actor. The claim consumes the handoff before the bindings are compared, so a failed exchange is a single attempt.

outputs.name: NativeHandoffController.routes
outputs.description: A new route table built on each routes() call with the four POST /api/auth/native/* keys; each handler calls the matching private method on this controller instance.

inputs.name: NativeHandoffController.constructor.options
